# Findmypast's British Newspaper Archive, searched 27 September 2026 on David's own subscription.
# Row 134 recorded it as "UNTOUCHED, AND THE SUBSCRIPTION IS PAID FOR" and predicted that a local
# paper would carry "marriage reports naming the whole wedding party". IT CARRIED TWO.
field
# ---------------- *** TWO INDEPENDENT REPORTS OF ONE WEDDING *** ----------------
*** THE DATE IS SATURDAY 31 OCTOBER 1914, AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD ONLY "QUARTER 4" ***
column2: The GRO index gives CASTLE-WEAR, Hitchin, Q4 1914, vol 3A p.1552 — a three-month window. THE CITIZEN (LETCHWORTH) of Friday 6 November 1914 says "last Saturday" and the HERTFORDSHIRE EXPRESS of Saturday 7 November 1914 says "on Saturday". BOTH RESOLVE TO 31 OCTOBER 1914, which was a Saturday. Two papers, two offices, one date.

column1: report 1 — Citizen (Letchworth), Fri 6 November 1914, page 4
column2: Military Wedding. There was a military wedding at the Congregational Church last Saturday. The bridegroom, Mr. HENRY ROBERT WEAR, of Letchworth, who was in full uniform, was married to Miss MARTHA MAUDE CASTLE (of Baldock). The Rev. T. Smith officiated.

column1: report 2 — Hertfordshire Express, Sat 7 November 1914, page 4, under a BALDOCK heading
column2: Soldier's Wedding. — At the Congregational Church on Saturday the wedding took place quietly of Miss MAUDE CASTLE, of NORTON STREET, and Mr. HARRY WARE, of Letchworth. The bridegroom was on furlough from BURY ST. EDMUNDS, the headquarters of the 1ST HERTS TERRITORIALS, to which he is attached. The Rev. T. Smith, pastor, officiated, and after a short stay the bridegroom REJOINED HIS REGIMENT, WHICH LATER RECEIVED ORDERS TO PROCEED TO THE FRONT.

column1: *** THE CHURCH: THE CONGREGATIONAL CHURCH AT BALDOCK ***
column2: the Citizen says only "the Congregational Church"; the Express prints it under a BALDOCK heading and names the Rev. T. Smith as PASTOR there. The Citizen's neighbouring item, "Call to Baldock Minister", is about the same man being called to Bicester. NOT A REGISTRY OFFICE AND NOT THE PARISH CHURCH — a Nonconformist chapel, which is a fact about the family and not only about the building.

column1: *** HER ADDRESS: NORTON STREET, BALDOCK ***
column2: the first address this archive has ever had for MARTHA MAUD CASTLE before her marriage. Row 134 listed "the Castles at Baldock and Norton" as a target and this answers it with a street rather than a village — NORTON STREET IS IN BALDOCK, and is not the neighbouring village of Norton.

column1: *** HE WAS ON FURLOUGH, AND THE BATTALION SAILED DAYS LATER ***
column2: He is "attached" to the 1st Herts Territorials with headquarters at BURY ST EDMUNDS, came home on furlough, married quietly, and rejoined. The 1/1st Battalion Hertfordshire Regiment landed in France on 6 NOVEMBER 1914 — the day the Citizen printed its notice. HE MARRIED ON A WEEK'S LEAVE AND WENT TO THE FRONT.

column1: the regiment was already known, and this corroborates it independently
column2: leonard.astro already carries his WO 363 record, service number 3010, Hertfordshire Regiment 1st Battalion 1914-18. THE NEWSPAPER IS NOT THE SOURCE OF THAT AND AGREES WITH IT — a service record and a village paper, written for different reasons, putting the same man in the same regiment in the same autumn.

column1: *** AND A NAME VARIANT WORTH HAVING: HARRY WARE ***
column2: the Express renders HENRY ROBERT WEAR as "Mr. HARRY WARE". A searcher looking for WEAR in these papers will not find him. This is the same lesson as Ivone's six spellings, on the English side.

column1: the wedding took place quietly
column2: the Express's own words. Two witnesses, no wedding party named, no bridesmaids, no breakfast — which is why there is no list of relatives here and why this row does not pretend there is.

column1: # ---------------- AND A SECOND FINDING, FROM A DIFFERENT SEARCH ----------------
*** 72 PIX ROAD WAS SOMEBODY ELSE'S HOUSE BY OCTOBER 1935 ***
column2: Searching the exact string "72 Pix Road" returns THREE articles in the whole corpus. One is a wedding report of Saturday 5 October 1935 in the Hertfordshire Express: "Miss Elsie Chapman, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. E. S. Chapman, of 72. Pix-road". THE OTHER TWO ARE A 1913 POST OFFICE THEFT CASE against Walter Harris, a postman living there before the Wears.

column1: so the move is bracketed from both ends now
column2: The 1921 census has HENRY ROBERT and MARTHA MAUD WEAR at 72 Pix Road; the 1939 Register has the household at 18 RIDGE AVENUE, Letchworth. THE CHAPMANS AT THE OLD ADDRESS IN OCTOBER 1935 NARROWS THE MOVE FROM "between 1921 and 1939" TO "between 1921 and October 1935". This archive claims only that; a wedding report gives the bride's parents' address and nothing about who held the tenancy in which year.

column1: # ---------------- *** A NEGATIVE, AND IT IS THE ONE ROW 134 MOST WANTED *** ----------------
*** MARTHA CASTLE'S DEATH OF 1863 IS NOT IN THE HERTFORDSHIRE PAPERS ***
column2: Row 134 hoped a Hertfordshire paper "may report MARTHA GIDDINGS' DEATH IN 1863 where a certificate is slow and costs money". FIRST, THE SEARCH STRING WAS WRONG IN THE ROW ITSELF: she died as MARTHA CASTLE, her married name, registered Q3 1863 at Hitchin, vol 3A p.188. Searching "martha giddings" returns 24 articles and not one is hers. Searching "martha castle" FILTERED TO COUNTY OF PUBLICATION = HERTFORDSHIRE returns THREE, and none is hers: a death notice of 25 April 1884 for a Martha Castle AGED 39, an inquest witness named Martha Castle Butler in 1862, and a court list of 1872.

column1: and the coverage control says the absence is real, though it is weak evidence
column2: THE 1862 ITEM IS FROM THE HERTFORDSHIRE EXPRESS, PUBLISHED AT HITCHIN — so a Hitchin paper is digitised and searchable for the exact period, and a death notice in 1863 COULD have been found. THE ABSENCE IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF COVERAGE. But it is weak evidence about anything: a labourer's wife dying in 1863 usually got no paid death notice, and Victorian papers printed the deaths of those who could pay. IT DOES NOT SEPARATE THE Q3 1863 MARTHA CASTLE FROM THE 1865 ONE, which is the ambiguity castle-giddings-1862.tsv left open, and that still needs the certificate.

column1: a SAMUEL CASTLE occupying a cottage in Norton Street, Baldock
column2: an undated property-sale notice found while searching Norton Street: "with Yard and Wood Barn to each, situate NORTON-STREET, in the occupation of James Beecher, SAMUEL CASTLE, and Elias Howard; Copyhold COTTAGES ... situated at NORTON END". NOT CLAIMED AS KIN. Castle is a common Baldock surname and the notice was not opened or dated. It is recorded because Martha Maud was living in Norton Street in 1914 and because NORTON END is where James Giddins, Derrick's 3x-great-grandfather, was living in the 1861 and 1871 censuses. Two streets, two families this archive descends from, one lead worth an hour later.
